newsitem.title: TANZANIA: No elections for Zanzibar before 2000 - president.
newsitem.headline: No elections for Zanzibar before 2000 - president.

text.p: Zanzibar president Salmin Amour has rejected opposition pressure for new elections in the semi-autonomous island, saying his government will remain in power until the year 2000 as scheduled.
Addressing a rally in Zanzibar, which is part of Tanzania, Amour said on Saturday his government would resist any attempt to force an early poll, the state-owned Sunday News reported.
In elections last October, Amour's ruling Chama cha Mapinduzi (Revolutionary) party defeated the Civic United Front (CUF) by a narrow majority, gaining 50.2 per cent of the votes.
Opposition allegations of election irregularities, backed by international humanitarian organisations, have led to some donors cutting aid to Zanzibar.

Zanzibar joined mainland Tanganyika to form the United Republic of Tanzania after the 1964 revolution which overthrew the last Arab Sultan of Zanzibar. It retains a large measure of autonomy, with its own government and parliament, and is also represented in the Tanzanian parliament.
